message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's latest 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy AAPL within your mandate. The filing shows fiscal 2024 net income of $93,736 million (down modestly from $96,995M in 2023), revenue of $391,035 million (+2%), operating income of $123,216 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million. The year-over-year net income decline was driven largely by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the EU State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), masking solid operating momentum: Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169 million and total gross margin expanded to 46.2%, with $140.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00 — very close to market — which filled for $9,812, comfortably below the $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, and with no money moved out of the account.
message.reasoning_content:
The order filled at $223.00 for 44 shares = $9,812. Within $10,000 per order, total today $9,812 < $20,000. Cash was $50,000, so sufficient (though now $40,188). Never moved money out. Good.
